paper_sections.title: Conflict processing modulated by global control context
Conflict processing modulated by local control context

description.value: An fMRI study comparing neural substrates of emotional versus non-emotional conflict modulation by global control context using face-word interference tasks with manipulated proportion congruent blocks and an independent face localizer.

spans.text: We addressed this aim in a functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) study that varied the proportion of congruent trials in emotional vs. non-emotional conflict tasks across blocks.

description.value: Twenty-four right-handed volunteers participated; three were excluded, leaving 21 participants. Participants completed emotional and non-emotional face-word conflict tasks and a subsequent independent face-versus-house localizer during fMRI. Task-domain, current congruency, proportion congruent, and previous-trial congruency were within-subject factors.

spans.text: Participants performed two tasks during fMRI: a face-word interference task (including an emotional and a non-emotional version), which was performed first, and a subsequent standard localizer task to provide independent functional definitions of the FFA and the amygdala as ROIs.

Structural images were acquired with a T1-weighted SPGR sequence using a 3D inversion recovery prepared sequence, recording 180 slices of 1 mm thickness in plane-resolution of 1 × 1 mm (  TR   = 7.48 ms,   TE   = 2.98 ms, field of view = 256 × 256 mm).

description.value: Functional images were slice-time corrected, realigned, coregistered with the structural image, normalized to MNI space, high-pass filtered, and spatially smoothed.

spans.text: Functional data were slice-time corrected and spatially realigned to the first volume of the first run. The structural scan was co-registered to the functional images, and served to calculate transformation parameters for spatially warping functional images to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) template brain (resampled voxel size: 2 mm ). Finally, normalized functional images were spatially smoothed with an 8 mm  full-width-half-maximum Gaussian kernel. The first 5 volumes of each run were discarded prior to building and estimating the statistical models. In order to remove low-frequency confounds, data were high-pass filtered (128 s).
All preprocessing and statistical analyses were carried out using SPM8 (  http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm/software/spm8/  ).

model_settings.value: Sixteen event regressors crossed task-domain, proportion congruent, previous-trial congruency, and current-trial congruency; error trials, first trials of blocks, and instruction screens were nuisance regressors. Temporal autocorrelation was modeled with AR-1 and restricted maximum likelihood variance-component estimates.

spans.text: This model was applied to each subject's data, followed by linear contrasts between events of interest.

estimator.value: maximum likelihood with restricted maximum likelihood variance-component estimation

spans.text: Temporal autocorrelations were estimated using restricted maximum likelihood estimates of variance components using a first-order autoregressive model (AR-1), and the resulting non-sphericity was used to form maximum likelihood estimates of the activations.
All preprocessing and statistical analyses were carried out using SPM8 (  http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm/software/spm8/  ).
